modes.label: COMIC
modes.keywords: vintage color comic, expressive brush inking, halftone shading, printed paper
modes.prompt: Redraw the supplied photo as a single vintage color-comic illustration. Use expressive brush-ink contours with varied line weight, broad shadow shapes, and selective cross-hatching. Build midtones from visible halftone dots and use a limited palette of warm red, mustard yellow, and muted blue on cream paper. Keep the main subjects crisply inked, with simpler shapes in the background; let paper texture sit beneath the ink without obscuring small features. Preserve individual facial features, expressions, clothing, and object shapes through confident hand-drawn simplification. Keep the original subjects, object count, poses, camera angle, crop, and background arrangement. Fill the frame with the illustration without added panels, lettering, or decoration. Lighting finish only: {context}.

modes.label: WATERCOLOR
modes.keywords: watercolor painted from scratch, blended wet-on-wet washes, visible brushstrokes and dabs, pigment granulation and speckles, soft bleeding edges
modes.prompt: Paint the scene from scratch in watercolor using the supplied photo as a reference, not as a photograph with a watercolor filter or texture overlay. Construct every subject and background form from visible brushstrokes, broad watery washes, irregular dabs, and small dots of deposited pigment. Let neighboring colors bleed and blend on wet cotton paper, with soft feathered edges, uneven blooms, pooled pigment, and granular speckles within the painted areas. Replace photographic microdetail and precise contours with loose brush-shaped suggestions; describe faces and objects with a few expressive marks rather than tracing them. Leave broken dry-brush strokes and paper gaps visible, with only occasional firmer accents. Keep colors recognizable with richer warm and cool mixtures. Preserve likeness, expressions, subjects, object count, poses, camera angle, crop, and background arrangement through the overall painted shapes. Use moderate artistic looseness, with blending and brushwork visible at small size. Lighting finish only: {context}.

modes.label: ANIME
modes.keywords: hand-drawn anime film still, precise linework, shaped cel shadows, painted backgrounds
modes.prompt: Redraw the supplied photo as a polished hand-drawn anime film still. Use precise, varied linework, confident two- or three-tone cel shading, and carefully placed highlights that describe each material. Preserve individual likeness and expressions while translating faces into expressive anime features with restrained proportions. Give hair and fabric clear grouped shapes and retain the distinguishing details of objects. Render the existing background with softer painted edges and quieter detail so the main subjects read clearly. Use rich but balanced local colors, clean separation of light and shadow, and readable dark areas. Keep the original subjects, object count, poses, camera angle, crop, and background arrangement; all stylization belongs to the existing scene. Lighting finish only: {context}.

modes.label: SURPRISE
modes.keywords: unhinged one-shot transformation, impossible materials, broken scale, violent color
modes.prompt: Detonate the supplied photo into this already chosen vision and do not pull it back: {variation}. Commit the whole frame. The same people stay recognizable, in the same pose, and then materials, scale, gravity, and the room are allowed to go too far. The palette is the world, not a tint. The focus choice decides what stays razor sharp and what becomes the storm. Do not make it tasteful, balanced, vintage, or politely photographic unless the treatment itself is a photograph pushed past sanity. No borders, lettering, or logos. Lighting is only a spark inside the vision: {context}.

modes.label: PENCIL SKETCH
modes.keywords: full-color pencil drawing, directional strokes, layered color, visible paper tooth
modes.prompt: Redraw the supplied photo as an expressive full-color colored-pencil sketch on ivory drawing paper. Build forms with fine directional strokes that follow their surfaces, layered colored hatching, and changes in pencil pressure. Choose pencil colors from the source image and deepen shadows with complementary colored layers so they stay chromatic. Let paper tooth show between strokes, reserve bare paper for highlights, and use a few softly burnished passages for smooth surfaces. Concentrate precise marks around the main subjects and use broader, looser strokes in the existing background. Preserve individual likeness, expressions, and recognizable object shapes without tracing every edge equally. Keep the original subjects, object count, poses, camera angle, crop, and background arrangement. Lighting finish only: {context}.

prompt_system:
Write one image-edit prompt for Grok Imagine from the supplied draft. For every style except surprise, refine its language without inventing creative content. Use roughly 100 to 160 words for those styles. For surprise, use up to 220 words if the treatment needs it, and do not tame, shorten, or make it tasteful. Do not pad short drafts.
Lead with the transformation of the supplied photograph. Spend most of the prompt on the selected medium, mark-making, material rendering, color relationships, and focal hierarchy. Describe physical qualities directly rather than generic quality adjectives.
Preserve the draft's distinctive treatment. For surprise, keep the selected treatment, palette, and focus and push them harder: impossible materials, broken scale, and a setting rewritten by that treatment are required. For every other style, keep photographic treatments photographic and illustrated treatments faithful to their stated medium.
You cannot see the photograph. For styles other than surprise, refer to its existing subjects and surroundings without naming or imagining unseen objects, and preserve likeness, expressions, object count, poses, camera angle, crop, and background arrangement. For surprise, keep the people recognizable and in the same pose, and let the treatment rewrite materials, scale, and the room.
The lighting finish is secondary. Combine its cues into at most one short sentence about exposure, color temperature, shadow softness, or reflected light on existing surfaces. For styles other than surprise, keep the original light direction and source materials, and if a cue conflicts with the style or scene, soften or omit it. For surprise, the treatment's materials and palette win over the original light.
For styles other than surprise, express lighting through the selected medium, keep interiors as interiors, preserve the existing sky or ceiling, and change only the rendering of existing content. Add no objects, scenery, symbols, decorative overlays, or lettering. Surprise may add the objects and scenery named by its selected treatment, and still no lettering.
Remove repeated instructions and negative keyword lists. Output only the finished edit prompt.
